translatedData.content:
With only a few hundred USDT of capital, to be honest, it’s better to be straightforward and follow the right direction.
With a few hundred USDT, you go for high-leverage futures. If you see which coin suddenly pumps, you chase in. If you lose, you think about averaging down to reduce your cost. At first, you might accidentally make a few trades. But once you truly run into a big market where things move strongly in the opposite direction, all the earlier profits get given back, and your principal goes to zero.$BTC 
So in the small-capital stage, the most important thing isn’t proving how capable you are—it’s first learning by following experienced people.
When I say “follow the big shots,” I don’t mean blindly copy trades, and I don’t mean handing your money over for someone else to manage. It means learning why they choose that position, why they control their position size, why they set stop-losses, and why they’re willing to stay in cash and wait.#ETH 
You’ll find that people who really trade for a long time actually don’t have that many actions. They won’t see a coin up 20% and rush in, and they won’t panic and cut losses just because it drops a few percent. They wait until the opportunity shows up. Only when the conditions are met do they act.
With a few hundred USDT, you don’t have much room for error. It can’t withstand repeated trial and error.
Rather than researching dozens of low-cap altcoins every day, it’s better to focus on a few mainstream coins first;
Rather than always thinking about doubling your money, it’s better to first learn how much loss on a single trade you must stop at;
Rather than constantly looking for a get-rich password, it’s better to truly learn a simple method and understand it well.
Small capital isn’t without opportunities—it just requires more patience.$SOL 
First learn the thinking from experts, then gradually form your own judgment. When one day you no longer rely on anyone’s calls, and you can judge the market yourself, control your position size, and execute your stop-loss—then you’ll truly be on your own trading path.
A few hundred USDT isn’t meant to risk your life—it’s money to pay tuition and build long-term cognition.
Follow me. No hype about getting rich overnight—just how to survive with small capital. #small-capital survival #trading learning

Revolut issues its own euro stablecoin: this time it’s not an exchange frenzy—it's payments giants stepping in

Revolut has officially launched the EURR stablecoin. The fintech giant with 30 million users has personally entered the on-chain euro payments game.

Revolut is one of Europe’s largest fintech apps, with a user base in the tens of millions. Now they’ve rolled out their own euro stablecoin, EURR, with a clear goal: embed stablecoin payments directly into the existing app experience. In plain terms: when you transfer or pay in Revolut, the underlying settlement may run on-chain—but users won’t perceive any blockchain at all. The logic is exactly the same as PayPal launching PYUSD: traditional finance players aren’t looking to trade crypto; they want to use stablecoins to lower settlement costs.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment-wise, it’s a positive. When major firms issue stablecoins, it effectively endorses the whole industry, and capital may expect more fintechs to follow. But EURR itself won’t directly create buy pressure for BTC/ETH—so don’t expect a pump today. BTC is currently $78,901.17, down 1.98% in the past 24 hours and in a pullback. This kind of news acts as a sentiment backstop, not a reversal engine.
- Medium term: the industry landscape is the real focus. The stablecoin race has shifted from the USDT/USDC duopoly into a three-way battle among “exchange-backed + payment-backed + bank-backed” players. Whoever controls the user relationship controls the issuance power. The more compliant euro stablecoins there are, the harder it becomes for European regulators to take a one-size-fits-all, blanket crackdown on Crypto—this is a long-term positive for the whole market.

My take
I’m bullish on the direction, but by layers: in the short term, BTC around $78,901.17 is likely still just ranging as it digests; this news alone isn’t enough to independently flip the weak 24-hour trend. For ETH, as the main infrastructure for stablecoin settlement, the mid-to-long-term benefit case is cleaner. If $2,459.32 holds and stabilizes, the upside elasticity could be better than the broader market. The real validation point will be the on-chain issuance growth rate of EURR: if within three months it jumps into the top two by euro stablecoin supply, the narrative for the sector will get another spark. The risk is that “fintech issuing tokens” ≠ “fintech driving token price.” Don’t confuse payment-side positivity with trading-side positivity.

Ethereum #ETH $ETH  is the world’s only, decentralized, Turing-complete financial computing infrastructure—it is not a currency, not an application, but “the operating system for the financial internet.”

Is this a good business?
 Yes—but not in the traditional sense of a “good business.” Ethereum is more like a public utility: it creates enormous economic value, but the value-capture mechanisms are not yet well-developed. Its moat—liquidity depth, developer ecosystem, institutional trust, and security track record—is the widest among all blockchains worldwide, and it is still widening.
Is it a good price?
 If your time horizon is 3–5 years, the stacked catalysts below could trigger a major valuation repricing: successful rollout of the Glamsterdam and Hegotá upgrades, the RWA tokenization market growing from $17B to many hundreds of billions of dollars, the scaling of staking-based ETFs attracting allocations from pension funds and sovereign wealth funds, and the CLARITY Act ultimately passing by eliminating regulatory uncertainty.
It’s recommended to gradually accumulate in the $2,200–$2,500 range, as a core allocation within the crypto infrastructure space. Focus on whether the 2026 Q4 Glamsterdam upgrade’s rollout shows measurable traction and whether L1 fee revenues show a turning point—this is a key observation window to validate the “value-capture repair” thesis.

Ceasefire Deal Reached Between Iran and the US Sparks Optimism for the Reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, Raising Expectations

The geopolitical situation in the Middle East has once again gripped global markets. According to several media reports citing information, the United States and Iran have made new progress regarding ceasefire arrangements and the issue of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and the crude oil market quickly reacted to the easing expectations.

As for the background, the US and Iran previously reached a related memorandum of understanding under Pakistan’s mediation, setting a framework for promoting a ceasefire and restoring shipping through the strait. However, due to disagreements over shipping routes and control of strait management, the framework was not smoothly renewed after its expiration. In recent weeks, Pakistan has continued intensive back-and-forth communication. A delegation led by Pakistan’s army chief visited Tehran, where it met with Iran’s president, speaker, foreign minister and other senior officials. The key topics included preventing escalation, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and accelerating the end of the conflict. Before the visit, senior Pakistani officials reportedly also held direct communication with the US, playing a role in transmitting signals both ways. Iranian media, meanwhile, emphasized that the trip aims to create room for negotiations and to convey Iran’s conditions and positions to the US.

On the core factual level, Russian media cited sources from Pakistan’s military and Iran’s security apparatus as saying that the US and Iran have reached consensus on the terms of a ceasefire agreement, with the free navigation of the Strait of Hormuz explicitly included. The sources said that both sides are expected to release related information in the coming days and initiate negotiations and technical meetings based on the earlier Islamabad memorandum of understanding. At the same time, Xinhua reported that on the 25th Iran and Oman issued a joint statement, proposing to establish a jointly agreed security maritime corridor in the Strait of Hormuz. The proposed framework includes setting up a secure shipping corridor, reaching joint arrangements for the corridor’s operation, establishing a coordination mechanism involving both countries’ coast guards, and continuing to coordinate on future management, information exchange, traffic management, and navigation safety services. The statement also stressed that talks should be held with other countries along the Persian Gulf coast, that applicable international law should be followed, and that the coastal states’ sovereignty and sovereign rights should be respected.

It should be noted that the above ceasefire consensus currently comes mainly from anonymous sources relayed by media, and the US and Iranian governments have not yet released the full text of the agreement. Iran’s deputy foreign minister said publicly that if the US wants the strait reopened, it must correct its mistakes and return to the earlier commitments. The conditions for reopening the strait also include a comprehensive end to fighting on all fronts, lifting blockades, and defusing the situation in relevant areas. Iran has conveyed its demands to the US through mediated channels, emphasizing that it must again comply with the provisions in the earlier memorandum regarding navigation rules for the strait, among other terms. Therefore, what the market is trading right now is the expectation of warming, not the reopening of the strait for large-scale normal traffic or the formal effectiveness of a ceasefire agreement.

Breaking down the logic, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz actually involves two parallel paths: one is the political and ceasefire negotiation pushed by Pakistan between the US and Iran; the other is the technical arrangement between Iran and Oman involving a temporary shipping corridor and coast-guard coordination. If the two finally connect, the risk of supply disruptions could decline. But if the ceasefire text is delayed, disagreements arise over fulfillment of commitments, or technical coordination proves hard to implement, the risk remains that earlier negotiations could fall apart. After the news surfaced, oil prices fell noticeably for a time, reflecting the market’s rapid digestion of the expectation that the geopolitical risk premium may fade.

In terms of how this affects the crypto market, the transmission is mostly indirect—through a shift in risk appetite. Reduced uncertainty in Middle East supply and shipping typically helps ease sharp swings in global inflation expectations and risk-aversion sentiment, thereby improving the overall environment for risk assets. Conversely, if later official narratives diverge or implementation repeatedly changes, risk-averse sentiment could rise again, affecting—including in high-volatility instruments such as digital assets—the timing and rhythm of capital flows. The crypto market itself does not directly track crude oil or strait navigation, but shifts in macro liquidity expectations, the linkage between the US dollar and commodity prices, and synchronized changes in investors’ risk preferences may still produce emotional-level correlation.

Editor’s assessment and observations: At present, the progress carries meaningful signals. The joint statement between Iran and Oman has moved from principle-level discussion to more concrete arrangements such as the corridor and coordination mechanisms, and Pakistan’s mediation has also reactivated the memorandum framework. However, before the formal text is released, the status of the US’s commitment fulfillment is clarified, and the actual scale of merchant-ship traffic through the strait returns to normal, it is still not advisable to treat the easing as a foregone conclusion. Over the next few days, the pace of official disclosures, whether the ceasefire terms cover multiple fronts, and how operational the temporary security corridor is will be key areas to watch. Facts and expectations must be separated: “consensus reportedly reached” is the current information, while implementation and the reopening remain unverified. Market sentiment is easily driven by headlines, so it is more important to rationally distinguish “negotiation progress” from “the end of the situation.”

美伊传就停火条款达成共识霍尔木兹复航预期升温

近期中东地缘局势再度牵动全球市场神经。据多家媒体援引消息，美国与伊朗围绕停火安排及霍尔木兹海峡通航问题出现新进展，原油市场迅速对缓和预期作出反应。

事件背景方面，美伊此前曾在巴基斯坦斡旋下达成过相关谅解备忘录，设定推动停火与恢复海峡航运的框架，但因航运路线与海峡管理权等分歧，该框架在到期后未能顺利续期。巴基斯坦方面近期持续穿梭沟通：巴陆军元帅率团访问德黑兰，会见伊朗总统、议长、外长等高层，讨论重点包括防止局势升级、重新开放霍尔木兹海峡以及加速终止冲突。访问前，巴方高层据称还与美方进行过直接沟通，扮演了双向传递信号的角色。伊朗媒体则强调，此行意在为谈判创造空间，并向美方转达伊方条件与立场。

核心事实层面，俄罗斯媒体援引巴基斯坦军方及伊朗安全部门消息人士称，美伊已就停火协议条款达成共识，其中明确纳入霍尔木兹海峡自由通航内容。消息人士表示，双方预计未来几天公布相关消息，并依据此前伊斯兰堡谅解备忘录启动谈判及技术性会议。与此同时，新华社报道，伊朗与阿曼25日发表联合声明，拟在霍尔木兹海峡建立一条双方共同商定的安全海上通道。拟议框架包括建立安全航运走廊、就走廊运行达成共同安排、设立两国海岸警卫队共同参与的协调机制，并继续就未来管理、信息交换、交通管理及航行安全服务保持协调。声明还强调应与波斯湾沿岸其他国家磋商，遵守适用国际法并尊重沿岸国主权权利。

需要指出的是，上述停火共识目前主要来自匿名消息人士转述，美伊官方尚未公布完整协议文本。伊朗副外长公开表示，若美方希望海峡重开，必须纠正错误并重回此前承诺；海峡重新开放的条件还包括全面结束各战线战事、解除封锁以及化解相关地区局势。伊方已通过斡旋渠道向美方传递要求，强调须重新遵守此前谅解备忘录中有关海峡航行规则等条款。因此，当前市场交易的是预期升温，而非海峡已恢复大规模正常通航或停火协议已正式生效。

逻辑拆解来看，霍尔木兹复航实际上出现两条并行路径：一条是巴基斯坦推动的美伊政治与停火谈判，另一条是伊朗与阿曼围绕临时航运走廊与海岸警卫协调的技术安排。若两者最终衔接，供应中断风险有望下降；但若停火文本公布延迟、承诺履行出现争议，或技术协调难以落地，此前谈判破裂的风险仍存。油价在消息传出后一度明显回落，反映市场迅速消化地缘风险溢价可能消退的预期。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多是间接的风险偏好传导。中东供应与航运不确定性下降，往往有助于缓和全球通胀与避险情绪的剧烈波动，从而改善风险资产整体环境；反之，若后续官方口径分歧或执行反复，避险情绪可能再度抬头，影响包括数字资产在内的高波动品种的资金节奏。加密市场本身并不直接锚定原油或海峡通航，但宏观流动性预期、美元与大宗商品联动，以及投资者风险偏好的同步变化，仍可能在情绪层面带来联动。

编辑判断与观察：目前进展具有实质信号意义，伊阿联合声明已从原则讨论推进到走廊与协调机制等具体安排，巴方斡旋也重新激活了备忘录框架。然而，在正式文本公布、美方承诺履行情况澄清以及商船实际通行规模恢复之前，仍不宜将缓和视为定局。未来几天官方信息披露节奏、停火条款是否覆盖多战线、以及临时安全通道的可操作性，将是观察重点。事实与预期必须分开：共识“据报达成”是当前信息，落地与复航仍是待验证过程。市场情绪易受标题驱动，理性区分“谈判进展”与“局势终结”更为重要。

Iran has disrupted operations in the Strait of Hormuz, paralyzing it; nearly half of global oil transport is affected

💡 Impact assessment: bullish in the short term 📈. The oil-price shock boosts safe-haven and hard-asset demand, while capital looks for a hedge against the yuan’s (fiat currency) depreciation by exporting and seeking out alternatives.

Iran’s conflict cuts off the Strait of Hormuz, with almost half of global oil transport disrupted. Inflation pressure is re-accelerating, and the hard-asset narrative is heating up.

What’s going on
The Strait of Hormuz is the throat of global oil transport. About 20 million barrels of crude oil pass through it every day, accounting for nearly half of global trade volume. Now shipping traffic has collapsed—oil tankers don’t dare to go, and insurance premiums have surged. Oil supply contracts → oil prices rise → global inflation pressure returns. The transmission path is very direct: inflation expectations rise → anxiety about fiat currency purchasing power → funds seek hard assets as a hedge. BTC, with its fixed total supply, is one of the destinations. At the same time, central banks’ room to cut rates is squeezed, but markets often price in the “safe haven + anti-inflation” logic first, before watching the central bank’s face.

Market impact
- Short term: both safe-haven funds and anti-inflation funds rush in from two sides. BTC is currently at $80,550.17 and is up 4.54% in 24h, suggesting the market is not treating this geopolitical shock as pure bearish news—it’s pricing in a premium for hard assets. ETH at $2,504.25 is up 2.19%; it’s tracking higher, but with weaker upside elasticity than BTC—typical of a safe-haven market structure.
- Medium term: if the strait blockade persists and oil prices stay high, US inflation data may worsen again. Rate cuts by the Federal Reserve would be delayed, which is tail risk for risk assets. But the historical pattern is: in the early phase of geopolitical conflicts, BTC’s safe-haven buying comes first; then, later, liquidity tightening accounting catches up.

My take
I’m bullish in the short term. BTC’s performance this time (+4.54%, clearly outperforming ETH) suggests the market is treating it as “digital gold” rather than a risk asset. The key is whether $80,550 can hold. If it holds, the safe-haven narrative continues, pushing toward the $84K area as resistance. If it breaks below the $78K support, it would indicate the safe-haven logic has given way to liquidity panic—that would mean a different script. The main risk is: if oil prices spiral out of control and drag down US equities, crypto will be hard to stand apart from the fallout. That’s the biggest downside variable.

One-sentence translation: oil supply disruption → inflation anxiety → money starts looking for homes outside fiat currency. BTC is the beneficiary.

霍尔木兹海峡是全球石油运输的咽喉，每天约2000万桶原油从这里过，占全球贸易量的近一半。现在航运交通量崩了，油轮不敢走、保险费飙升。石油供给收缩→油价上行→全球通胀压力回来了。传导路径很直接：通胀预期升温→法币购买力焦虑→资金找硬资产对冲，BTC这类固定总量资产就是目的地之一。同时各国央行的降息空间被压缩，但市场往往先交易“避险+抗通胀”逻辑，再看央行脸色。

对市场的影响
- 短期：避险资金和抗通胀资金两头涌。BTC现报$80,550.17，24h已经涨了4.54%，说明市场没有把这次地缘冲突当成纯利空，反而在定价“硬资产溢价”。ETH $2,504.25涨2.19%，跟涨但弹性弱于BTC，典型的避险行情结构。
- 中期：如果海峡封锁持续，油价居高不下，美国通胀数据会重新恶化，美联储降息推迟，这对风险资产是尾部风险。但历史规律是：地缘冲突初期BTC避险买盘先行，后面才轮到流动性紧缩的账。

我的判断
我短期看多。这次BTC的表现（+4.54%，明显跑赢ETH）说明市场在把它当“数字黄金”交易，而不是风险资产。关键看$80,550能不能站稳——守住这里，避险叙事延续，冲击$84K一线阻力；一旦跌破$78K支撑，说明避险逻辑让位于流动性恐慌，那就要换剧本了。风险点是：如果油价失控把美股拖下水，加密很难独善其身，这是最大的反向变量。

一句话翻译：石油断供→通胀焦虑→钱开始找法币以外的家，BTC是受益方。

After BTC finished rising 80,000, it started to pull back. Generally ETH should soften too. But it hasn’t clearly been dragged down with it; it’s been chopping around on its own around 2,460. Entry is at 2,441, trailing stop-loss at 2,449, and take-profit 1 sits right around 2,464. Above that are 2,487 and 2,510. Several key levels are squeezed into a very narrow range. The short-term move has shifted from the earlier one-way rebound to longs and shorts choosing a direction.

The move up from the lower levels actually has some strength—there are fairly continuous bullish candles, and the shorts haven’t been able to immediately crush the rebound back down. Once price got to around 2,460, the push speed noticeably slowed. There’s still upside room, but it hasn’t been able to break higher for a while. This kind of pattern usually means either it’s regrouping here and later tries again at 2,487 and 2,510, or the support ultimately can’t hold and it gives back this whole rebound.

On a larger structure, the higher-level convergence looks even stronger. It’s more like waiting for the external market to break out, or for the market to send a resolution signal itself—not like a trend that’s already confirmed and running.

My own approach is pretty direct: I treat a move above 2,460 first as a corrective repair, but I won’t size in too heavily, since the space is tight and the turning point comes quickly. If it effectively drops back below 2,449, then I’ll treat this rebound as failed—reduce position or even flip direction. Conversely, if price reclaims and holds, and can push toward the 2,487 area, then consider adding in along with it. Let’s be real: having the stop-loss and the condition for switching set in advance is better than waiting and making an impulsive decision while watching the chart. The U.S. Department of the Treasury Sets Up a Quantum-Ready Task Force to Advance Anti-Quantum Migration

The U.S. Department of the Treasury has announced the formation of a Quantum-Ready Task Force—also referred to as a Quantum Security Preparedness Task Force. Its core objective is to help the U.S. financial industry transition to anti-quantum security technologies in an orderly manner that maintains operational resilience. The initiative uses a public-private cooperation framework led by the Treasury, bringing together government agencies, financial institutions, financial market infrastructure, technology providers, and other private-sector stakeholders to advance preparations related to post-quantum cryptography.

Public information indicates that Treasury Secretary Bessent said the task force will work to ensure the financial system remains secure, stable, and competitive in the face of disruptions caused by new technologies. The task force plans to carry out its work through three tracks: (1) industry coordination and migration to post-quantum cryptography; (2) preparedness of third parties and vendors; and (3) risks related to digital assets and emerging technologies. It will also align with the Group of Seven (G7) network experts group’s roadmap on post-quantum cryptography migration, with a focus on identifying key dependencies, improving cryptographic agility and interoperability, and strengthening the protection of critical financial infrastructure.

The backdrop to this development is not complicated. The current financial system relies heavily on traditional cryptographic algorithms such as public-key encryption to protect data, payments, identity authentication, and market infrastructure. The U.S. Treasury has noted that once quantum computing capabilities mature, they could, in theory, weaken or even break parts of today’s encryption systems, posing a long-term threat to financial data, payment systems, digital identities, and market infrastructure. Therefore, preparing early for the transition to post-quantum cryptography is positioned as a key measure to maintain economic security and the resilience of the financial system, rather than a slogan for short-term emergency response.

From a logical breakdown, the key difficulty in the quantum security agenda is not “whether to pay attention,” but “how to migrate with minimal friction.” Replacing post-quantum cryptography involves standardizing algorithms, ensuring system compatibility, coordinating across institutions, and modifying the supply chain. If financial institutions each act on their own, it is easy to end up with inconsistent standards, fragmented interfaces, and misaligned upgrade windows. If third-party software, cloud services, and outsourced vendors are ignored, gaps are likely to remain in the weakest link. By placing industry migration, vendor preparedness, and emerging-technology risks side by side, the approach suggests that the regulatory side is more inclined to treat quantum security as a systemic engineering effort rather than a single-technology procurement issue. Aligning with the G7 roadmap can also help reduce rule fragmentation across international financial activities.

In terms of how the change will affect the encryption market, the impact is more likely to show up at the levels of infrastructure, compliance expectations, and technical pathways. The task force explicitly includes digital-asset and emerging-technology risks on its agenda, which implies that scenarios such as on-chain asset custody, stablecoin settlement, exchange wallets, cross-system identity and signature verification may, in the future, be placed within a more comprehensive security assessment framework. In the long run, this could drive the industry to discuss earlier cryptographic agility upgrades, anti-quantum signature solutions, and smooth upgrade paths for critical systems. It is also important to separate facts from assumptions: what is confirmed by currently available public information is that the task force has been established, its task direction, and its attention to risks related to digital assets. This does not mean that a mandatory migration timeline has already been issued for a particular token generation or a specific type of protocol, nor does it constitute direct evidence of a short-term market catalyst.

In terms of editorial judgment, this matter is closer to forward-looking risk management and standards coordination rather than any immediate regulatory crackdown or a bullish narrative. For market observers, three areas are likely most worth tracking next: whether the post-quantum migration produces actionable, phased guidance; how third-party and vendor security requirements flow through to fintech and digital-asset service providers; and whether public-private cooperation can truly improve interoperability rather than remaining at the level of principle-based statements. Overall, the agenda for traditional financial security is extending into the post-quantum era, and the long-term technical foundation discussions for the crypto ecosystem may also be brought into a more formal policy framework as a result.

美国财政部成立量子就绪工作组推进抗量子迁移

美国财政部近日宣布成立量子就绪工作组，亦被表述为量子安全准备工作组，核心目标是推动美国金融业以有序且具备运营韧性的方式，向抗量子安全技术过渡。该机制采用公私合作框架，由财政部牵头，汇聚政府机构、金融机构、金融市场基础设施、技术供应商及其他私营部门力量，共同推进后量子密码相关准备。

公开信息显示，财政部长贝森特表示，工作组将努力确保金融体系在新技术冲击下仍能保持安全、稳定和竞争力。工作组拟通过三条工作线展开：一是行业协同与后量子密码迁移；二是第三方与供应商准备度；三是数字资产和新兴技术风险。同时，其将衔接七国集团网络专家组关于后量子密码迁移的路线图，重点识别关键依赖、提高密码敏捷性与互操作性，并强化关键金融基础设施保护。

事件背景并不复杂。现行金融体系大量依赖公钥加密等传统密码算法，用于保护数据、支付、身份认证和市场基础设施。美国财政部指出，一旦未来量子计算能力成熟，理论上可能削弱甚至破解部分现行加密体系，从而对金融数据、支付系统、数字身份和市场基础设施构成长期威胁。因此，提早布局后量子密码过渡，被定位为维护经济安全与金融体系韧性的关键准备，而非短期应急口号。

从逻辑拆解看，量子安全议题的关键难点不在“是否需要关注”，而在“如何低摩擦迁移”。后量子密码替换涉及算法标准化、系统兼容、跨机构协同和供应链改造。金融机构若各自为政，容易出现标准不一、接口割裂和升级窗口错配；若忽略第三方软件、云服务和外包供应商，则会在最薄弱环节留下缺口。把行业迁移、供应商准备与新兴技术风险并列，说明监管侧更倾向把量子安全当作系统性工程，而不是单一技术采购问题。与G7路线图衔接，则有助于减少跨国金融业务中的规则碎片化。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多体现在基础设施、合规预期和技术路线层面。工作组明确将数字资产和新兴技术风险纳入议程，意味着链上资产托管、稳定币结算、交易所钱包、跨系统身份与签名验证等场景，未来可能被置于更完整的安全评估框架中。长期看，这可能推动行业更早讨论密码敏捷性改造、抗量子签名方案以及关键系统的平滑升级路径。需要把事实与推断分开：目前公开信息确认的是工作组成立、任务方向和对数字资产风险的关注，并不等于已经出台针对某一代币或某类协议的强制迁移时间表，也不构成短期行情催化的直接证据。

编辑判断上，此事更接近前瞻性风险管理与标准协同，而不是即时监管打压或利好叙事。对市场观察者而言，后续更值得跟踪三方面：后量子迁移是否形成可执行的阶段性指引；第三方与供应商安全要求如何传导至金融科技和数字资产服务商；以及公私合作能否真正提高互操作性，而不是停留在原则性表态。整体看，传统金融安全议程正向抗量子时代延伸，加密生态的长期技术底座讨论，也可能因此被一并拉入更正式的政策视野。

Revolut launches euro stablecoin in three European countries: traditional finance finally really pays up—this isn’t just hype

Revolut has rolled out Bridge-issued EURR stablecoin across three European markets, aiming to cover the entire EEA within the year.

One of Europe’s largest financial apps, with a user base of 50 million+, has officially launched the euro stablecoin EURR in three European markets. The issuer is Bridge (the same company acquired by Stripe for $1.1 billion), and it supports multiple chains and external wallets. This will be expanded to cover the whole European Economic Area by year-end.

In plain terms, this is no longer a crypto-company issuing tokens—it’s a licensed financial giant treating stablecoins as a product line. Users can directly hold and transfer the euro stablecoin inside the Revolut app, which means crypto payments have, for the first time, reached ordinary European users in the guise of “legitimate banking features.”

Impact on the market
- Short term: BTC is at $78,614.79 (24h -1.64%), ETH at $2,454.53 (24h -1.24%), and the market sentiment itself is on the weak side. This news doesn’t directly lift the broader market, but the stablecoin narrative is a positive emotional variable. The wider the European regulatory-compliance pathway, the fewer worries there are for off-exchange capital.
- Medium term: The implications for the overall landscape are significant. The USD stablecoin track has already become a crowded red sea, and the euro stablecoin has long been missing a heavyweight player. Revolut’s user base + Bridge’s compliance infrastructure effectively opens a compliant on/off-ramp for fiat in Europe. In the next phase, it’s highly likely more licensed institutions will follow; stablecoin supply expansion is a fairly certain trend.

My take
Slightly bullish overall. In the short term, BTC is consolidating around $78,600; this news isn’t enough to reverse the weakness of -1.64%, so don’t expect a single green candle. But looking out to the medium term, every expansion of stablecoin infrastructure is a net inflow to the entire crypto market. I like this direction, but I’ll also be clear: regulatory-compliant capital is a slow variable—measured in quarters, not days. The risk is that Europe’s regulatory details haven’t been fully implemented yet, and the timeline to expand to the EEA could be delayed.

The Trump administration’s new sanctions are the first to list digital assets as targets for crackdown. Iran’s mining-based channel to bypass sanctions is about to be shut down.

This week, the Iranian rial in the public market fell to a historic low of about 2,020,000 rials per 1 USD. The trigger was that in Trump’s new sanctions proposal, digital assets were explicitly listed as a sanction target for the first time. For years, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has relied on a channel worth tens of billions of dollars—bitcoin mining—to get around oil sanctions: cheap domestic electricity for mining → mined BTC liquidated in international markets → exchanging currencies while bypassing the USD system.

One-sentence translation into a transmission chain: sanctions block Iran’s BTC liquidation channel → Iranian entities related to the selling of BTC for dollars to respond to dwindling foreign exchange reserves → near-term BTC catch-up bids face pressure.

If sanctions become long-term, it will weaken parts of the narrative of “using BTC to bypass sanctions at the state level,” and institutional capital may grow more concerned about compliance. However, it could also push U.S. regulation toward greater clarity—by blocking illicit uses, it may actually pave the way for compliant capital to enter.

What happened

In its latest round of sanctions, the Trump administration first listed digital assets as a target for crackdown, aiming directly at the IRGC (Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps) and a Bitcoin mining business worth billions of dollars. The logic is simple: after Iran was kicked out of SWIFT, BTC mined locally became one of the last channels to bypass the dollar system and obtain foreign exchange. 3. In trading, watch two things
First, the index: when it retraces, if it quickly washes back toward around 50, that’s a healthy shakeout—actually an opportunity to look for entries by finding the right spot. Second, who regains ground first: does BTC stabilize first, or do altcoins stabilize first? That determines whether the next cycle is a mainstream coin rally or a “catch-up” rally.

💡 Conclusion
Put simply: sentiment is in greed while price is pulling back—this isn’t a breakdown scenario; it’s a cooling-off scenario. My view is very clear: defend in the short term, scale in during pullbacks; once the Greed Index washes back into the neutral zone, consider increasing position size again. According to CoinTelegraph, U.S. spot BTC ETFs have just sparked a rush of seven consecutive days of net inflows. The impact is very direct: the year-to-date net outflow gap since early 2026 has been cut by more than half.

Here’s where the progress bar stands now: this batch of funds is still $390 million short of the historical record for the single month of net inflows in October 2025. In other words, with another decent run of weekly inflows, the record could be tied—or even refreshed.

One-sentence translation: The Wall Street money that retreated in the first half of this year is queuing up to come back.

Market impact
Short term: Liquidity has clearly improved, but the price action hasn’t caught up yet—BTC is currently at $79,029.46 (24h -1.87%), ETH at $2,466.12 (-1.32%), while SOL and XRP are falling even harder, down more than 4%. ETF buy pressure and coin prices are temporarily diverging; this kind of divergence is usually resolved by the coin price catching up, not by another round of capital pullbacks.

Medium term: ETFs have shifted from being a “net outflow drag” to a “net inflow engine.” Narrative switching matters more than day-to-day inflows. If the gap turns positive and replicates the October 2025 rhythm, the institutional allocation logic can stand back on its feet.

My take
I’m moderately bullish. One reason: seven straight days of net inflows isn’t retail sentiment—it’s sustained institutional behavior, and it’s happening while the price is moving sideways and falling. Buying more as it dips—that structure is healthy.

On price: if BTC holds the $79,000 area, the divergence between ETF flows and the market is likely to converge upward. The risk is this: if next week’s inflows pause and flip to net outflows, the divergence logic would fail and the room for a pullback would reopen. Iran unilaterally announced that ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz require permission, which increases the oil price risk premium; negative risk-off sentiment is further intensifying.

Iran has publicly declared that it exercises control over the Strait of Hormuz and requires all vessels to obtain permission in advance. This strait is the most critical chokepoint for global oil transportation, through which about 20% of the world’s oil trade passes. In plain terms, this is not a military operation—it’s a political signaling move. Iran is telling the outside world: I have the ability to choke the lifeline of global energy. Escalation of regional tensions is almost inevitable.

Impact on the market
The transmission path is straightforward: Strait controlled → risk premium on oil prices rises → inflation expectations tick up → markets worry the Fed will find it harder to cut rates → pressure builds on risk assets.

- Medium term: If Iran really intercepts ships, oil prices could spike plus inflation could rebound, rate-cut expectations would effectively go to zero, and the medium-term valuation logic for crypto would be directly undermined.

My view
Bearish, but it’s a “risk-event-driven selloff,” not a trend reversal. On the daily timeframe, BTC has support around $76,000; only if it breaks below that level is there room for further downside. I woke up and $BTC had already traded 1.521 billion USDT.

It’s down 2 points—so little volume.

Something’s off.

Not a panic sell-off with heavy volume.

And not the kind of dead silence where nobody’s playing.

In the past, I always blamed myself for not being smart enough.

Last night I couldn’t sleep, tossing and turning, going over it again and again.

I missed wave after wave.

Later I finally figured it out.

Turns out I’m actually too smart.

I always try to find that one optimal solution.

The best entry price, the most perfect position size, the most comfortable stop-loss.

I keep calculating, and waiting, and waiting.

In the end, I could only watch the market slip right past my eyes.

Today, this setup just happened to smack me in the face.

$BTC 79,086, in the last 24 hours it’s down 2.05%, and the volume is still 1.521 billion.

Nobody on either side is sure.

If this were in the past, I would definitely try to figure it all out before making a move.

Now I understand—there’s no such thing as an optimal solution.

Every time I say, “Wait a bit longer,” I’m just making excuses for my hesitation.

As for where it goes next, I don’t have a clue.

#BTC #ETH #投资哲学 #交易心态 #CryptoCircle
